outline.chapter_title: Introduction: Motivation for Low-bit Large Language Models
outline.description: Introduce the rise of large language models, the computational and environmental costs of scaling, and why low-bit quantization is a promising direction. Present the main claim of the paper — BitNet b1.58 — and the pedagogical goals of the textbook.
sections: Growth of LLMs and computational trends
Costs of scaling: latency, memory, throughput, and energy
Quantization as a solution: overview and taxonomy
From FP16 to 4-bit and beyond: industry trends
Introducing BitNet b1.58: claims and high-level contributions
How to use this book: prerequisites and learning goals

outline.chapter_title: Technical Background: Transformers, LLM Architectures, and Computation Profile
outline.description: Provide a concise but rigorous review of the Transformer architecture and compute/parameter characteristics of LLMs. Explain which parts of models dominate runtime and energy so that the motivation for low-bit weight/activation representations becomes clear.
sections: Recap of the Transformer block: self-attention and feed-forward
Linear layers, matrix multiplication, and where FLOPs go
Parameter distribution: embeddings, attention, MLPs
Common normalization and nonlinear components (RMSNorm, SwiGLU)
The LLaMA architecture and why it is a popular backbone
Profiling compute and memory: which operations dominate inference and training

outline.chapter_title: Quantization Fundamentals and Low-bit Neural Networks
outline.description: Teach core quantization concepts needed to understand low-bit LLMs, including uniform vs non-uniform quantization, symmetric/asymmetric schemes, activation quantization, post-training quantization (PTQ) and quantization-aware training (QAT). Discuss common pitfalls and metrics for quantized models.
sections: Quantization basics: scale, zero point, dynamic range
Uniform vs non-uniform and per-channel vs per-tensor quantization
Activation quantization: ranges and token-wise scaling
PTQ (post-training quantization) vs QAT (quantization-aware training)
Ternary and binary networks: historical perspective and key techniques
Straight-through estimator and gradient handling for discrete weights
Error metrics for quantization: signal-to-quantization-noise, perplexity impact

outline.chapter_title: Prior Work: 1-bit Models, BitNet and Related Efforts
outline.description: Survey previous work that led to BitNet b1.58: BitNet, Ladder kernels, GPTQ, AWQ, other 2/4-bit methods, and hardware-oriented efforts. Explain what each prior approach contributes and its limitations.
sections: Overview of BitNet: architecture and core ideas
Post-training quantization methods: GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant
Low-bit kernels and system-level optimizations: Ladder and 2-bit kernels
Hardware initiatives and bespoke accelerators for low-bit compute
Limitations of past methods and the opportunity for ternary weights

outline.chapter_title: BitNet b1.58: Design Principles and Architecture
outline.description: Present a detailed description of BitNet b1.58: ternary weight design, int-add matrix multiplication paradigm, activation handling, and adoption of LLaMA-style components. Explain architectural changes compared to standard Transformers and original BitNet.
sections: What does '1.58 bits' mean? Ternary weights and entropy calculation
Design goals: accuracy parity with FP16, reduced energy & memory
BitLinear: replacing nn.Linear with low-bit multiply-free operations
Int-add matrix multiplication paradigm and computational implications
Activation quantization choices: 8-bit activations and token-wise scaling
LLaMA-alike components: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, rotary embeddings, bias removal
Where embeddngs live: full-precision embeddings and why

outline.description: Dive deep into the quantization function used by BitNet b1.58 — the absmean quantizer and its implementation. Explain scaling, rounding, clipping, and per-token activation scaling. Give mathematical exposition and intuition for stability and representational power.
sections: Mathematical definition of absmean quantization
Computing the scale parameter gamma and the role of epsilon
RoundClip function: rounding behavior and clipping rationale
Why include zero? Role of sparsity and feature filtering
Activation scaling to [-Qb, Qb] per token vs zero-point schemes
Implementation details: numerical stability and backpropagation
Alternatives and why absmean was chosen: empirical and theoretical reasons

outline.chapter_title: Training BitNet b1.58: Datasets, Optimization, and Practicalities
outline.description: Explain the training recipe used in the paper: datasets, token counts, hyperparameters, and optimization strategies for training from scratch with ternary weights. Discuss practical issues and best practices when training low-bit LLMs.
sections: Training data: RedPajama and public corpora; cleaning and deduplication
Training budgets: 100B tokens baseline and experiments with 2T tokens
Model sizes investigated: 3B, 3.9B, 7B, 13B, 30B, 70B
Optimization: optimizers, learning rates, warmup and schedules
Quantization-aware training techniques: STE, clamping, and regularization
Checkpointing and mixed-precision considerations
Training-from-scratch vs finetuning: trade-offs and when to use each

outline.description: Provide a system-level treatment of implementing BitNet b1.58. Cover kernel design, memory layout, frameworks integration (FasterTransformer, HuggingFace, vLLM, llama.cpp), and device-level considerations for latency and throughput.
sections: BitLinear kernel design: packing ternary weights and int-add routines
Using the Ladder 2-bit kernel in practice
Memory layout and DRAM-to-SRAM bandwidth considerations
Integrating with FasterTransformer for latency measurement
Adapting HuggingFace models and inference servers (vLLM, llama.cpp)
Dealing with embeddings and mixed precision at inference time
Practical debugging, profiling, and measuring single-token latency

outline.chapter_title: Evaluation: Tasks, Metrics, and Experimental Methodology
outline.description: Detail the evaluation suite, metrics, and methodology used in the experiments: perplexity, zero-shot tasks, validation datasets, and how to fairly compare to FP16 baselines.
sections: Perplexity as a primary measure for LM quality: WikiText2, C4
Zero-shot evaluation tasks: ARC, Hellaswag, Winogrande, PIQA, OpenbookQA, BoolQ, SciQ, LAMBADA
Evaluation harness: lm-evaluation-harness and standard protocols
Measuring latency, memory usage, and throughput: hardware setup
Energy estimation methodology and arithmetic energy models
Fair comparison practices: same tokens, model size parity and baselines

outline.description: Present and interpret the empirical results reported in the paper. Analyze perplexity and zero-shot performance across sizes, training token experiments, latency/memory/energy comparisons, and show where BitNet b1.58 achieves parity or advantage over FP16 LLaMA models.
sections: Perplexity results across model sizes and interpretation
Zero-shot task performance: scaling of gap with model size
When BitNet b1.58 matches FP16: thresholds and practical implications
Latency and GPU memory comparisons: speedups and memory reductions
Throughput experiments: 70B model on 2x80GB A100s and batch scaling
Energy savings analysis: arithmetic energy breakdown and total estimates
Token-scaling experiment: results with 2T tokens and StableLM comparison
Summary of Pareto improvements and mapping equivalences across precisions

outline.description: Analyze the ablation experiments and design choices to provide deeper insight into what matters for preserving accuracy in ternary LLMs. Explain the importance of zero, activation bitwidth, scaling choices, and kernel optimizations.
sections: Effect of including zero in the ternary set vs binary weights
Activation bitwidth ablations: 8-bit vs lower/higher
Quantizer variants: absmean vs alternatives and their effects
Embedding precision ablation: impact of keeping embeddings in FP16
Kernel optimizations and their marginal gains for latency
Sensitivity to training tokens and regularization choices
Practical takeaways for model designers

outline.chapter_title: Performance Characterization: Latency, Memory, Throughput, and Energy
outline.description: Provide an in-depth systems analysis of why BitNet b1.58 provides the observed gains. Detail where time and energy is spent, how gains scale with model size, and how system-level choices (e.g., pipeline parallelism) influence outcomes.
sections: Profiling breakdown: compute vs memory-bound stages
Why speedups grow with model size: analysis of nn.Linear scaling
Memory footprint trends and the role of embedding size
Throughput analysis under batching and pipeline parallelism
Energy model: arithmetic energy per operation and chip-level estimates
Putting it together: latency-memory-energy trade-off curves
Design implications for system architects and operators

outline.chapter_title: Applications, Deployment Considerations, and Use Cases
outline.description: Discuss practical applications and deployment scenarios enabled by BitNet b1.58: MoE models, long-context LLMs, edge/mobile deployments, and when to choose ternary models in production.
sections: 1-bit Mixture-of-Experts: memory and communication benefits
Handling long context: reduced KV cache memory and token scaling
Edge and mobile deployment: CPU friendliness and resource constraints
Real-world inference pipelines: batch sizing, latency SLOs, and fail-safes
Safety, robustness and calibration considerations for low-bit LLMs
Economic and environmental implications of deploying 1.58-bit models

outline.description: Explore hardware implications and future research directions: design of specialized accelerators for 1-bit LLMs, further quantization/compression, alternative training recipes, and open research questions.
sections: Why new hardware matters: LPUs and multiply-free compute units
Hardware design primitives: int-add arrays, memory hierarchies, and bandwidth
Opportunities for further compressing activations and KV caches
Research directions: 1-bit MoE, adaptive precision, and mixed-precision kernels
Open challenges: training stability, sparsity exploitation, and model interpretability
Benchmarks and standardization needs for low-bit LLM evaluation

outline.chapter_title: Practical Guide: From Research to Production
outline.description: Provide a pragmatic, hands-on guide for engineers and researchers to reproduce and deploy BitNet b1.58-style models: code integration tips, measurement checklists, and troubleshooting.
sections: Reproducing experiments: required compute and reproducibility checklist
Converting an FP16 model to ternary (when applicable) vs training-from-scratch
Integrating with FasterTransformer, vLLM and llama.cpp: step-by-step notes
Measuring latency, memory, throughput, and energy reliably
Common pitfalls and debugging strategies
Operational considerations: monitoring, update workflows, and rollbacks

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Considerations and the New Scaling Law
outline.description: Formalize the notion of a 'scaling law' for 1.58-bit LLMs introduced in the paper. Discuss how effective model capacity, compute, and token budgets interact with precision, and provide theoretical intuition for the observed equivalence mappings (e.g., 13B b1.58 ~ 3B FP16).
sections: Review of conventional scaling laws for LLMs
Defining effective bits and model capacity for quantized networks
Empirical scaling observations in BitNet b1.58 and mapping rationale
A toy theoretical model connecting precision, parameter count and perplexity
Implications for optimal resource allocation under cost constraints
Limitations of the scaling law and where it may break down

outline.chapter_title: Appendices: Math, Code Snippets, and Experimental Artifacts
outline.description: Collect supporting materials: derivations, energy calculation details, dataset specifics, hyperparameter tables, code examples, and pointers to repositories used in research.
sections: Derivation details for absmean quantizer and related formulas
Energy model computations and data sources
Detailed training hyperparameters and schedules used in experiments
Dataset descriptions and preprocessing pipelines (RedPajama, C4, WikiText2)
Example kernel pseudo-code and packing formats for ternary weights
Links and notes for FasterTransformer, Ladder, HuggingFace, vLLM and llama.cpp
Further reading and bibliography
